title: Navratri and the Devi Calendar
intro: The major Devi observances. Dates are computed for your selected location by the app's panchang engine, never hard-coded.
editorialNote: Editorial content authored for this app. It has not been through independent scholarly review. See the Content Verification page.

observances.name: Sharad (Shardiya) Navratri
observances.summary: The principal nine-night observance, ending in Vijayadashami. The Saptashati is recited in full across the nine days in most traditions.
practices: Saptashati path (one charitra per day, or one chapter per day)
Kanya/Kumari puja on Ashtami or Navami
Havan on Navami in many traditions

observances.name: Chaitra Navratri
observances.summary: The spring Navratri. In Maharashtra and Andhra/Telangana/Karnataka its first day is Gudi Padwa / Ugadi, the new year.
practices: Ram Navami falls on the ninth day

observances.name: Gupt Navratri
observances.months: Magha and Ashadha shukla paksha (January–February and June–July)
observances.summary: The 'hidden' Navratris, observed particularly by tantric and sadhaka traditions and less publicly marked. Magha Gupt Navratri and Ashadha Gupt Navratri are reckoned separately.

observances.name: Vijayadashami / Dussehra
observances.summary: The tenth day. Marks Durga's victory over Mahishasura and, in the Rama tradition, Rama's victory over Ravana. Ayudha puja and Vidyarambham are common in the south.

observances.name: Bengali Durga Puja
observances.summary: The largest public festival of Bengal. Clay images made for the occasion, pandal visiting, and immersion on Dashami.

observances.name: Gujarat: Garba and Dandiya
observances.summary: Nine nights of circle dance around the garbo or the image of Amba, with fasting and the nine-colour convention.

observances.name: South India: Golu / Bommala Kolu
observances.summary: Stepped displays of dolls in homes, with songs, visiting and exchange of gifts. Ayudha puja and Saraswati puja fall within the same days.

observances.name: Kanya / Kumari Puja
observances.summary: Young girls are worshipped as forms of the Goddess. The practice and its details vary considerably by region and family.
practices: Nine girls for nine forms in many traditions

observances.name: Durga Ashtami and Maha Navami
observances.summary: The ritual peak of the nine days in most north Indian traditions. Havan is performed on Navami in many families; sandhi puja marks the Ashtami-Navami junction in Bengal.
